court: Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has Article III and statutory jurisdiction over the class and any habeas components.

issues.label: §1252(f)(1) scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether 8 U.S.C. §1252(f)(1) bars class-wide relief and whether it reaches declaratory judgments as well as injunctions.

issues.label: §1252(f)(1) relief characterization
issues.why: The court must determine whether the requested declaration would functionally operate as prohibited injunctive relief.

issues.label: Other §1252 limits
issues.why: The court must assess any additional jurisdiction-channeling or review-limiting provisions in §1252 that could restrict the claims or remedies.

issues.label: Sovereign immunity waiver
issues.why: The court must ensure a valid cause of action and waiver (e.g., APA/Ex parte Young-style, habeas, or constitutional equitable action) supports declaratory relief against the government.

issues.label: Proper defendants
issues.why: The court must confirm the named federal officials/entities are proper parties for the relief sought and have authority to implement it.

issues.label: Venue and personal jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must ensure proper venue and jurisdiction over defendants for class-wide declaratory relief.

issues.label: Standing (named plaintiff)
issues.why: The court must decide whether Onosamba-Ohindo has standing given his release and the nature of requested prospective relief.

issues.label: Mootness (individual claim)
issues.why: The court must determine whether plaintiff’s release moots his individual claims for prospective relief or declaratory relief.

issues.label: Inherently transitory exception
issues.why: The court must decide whether the claims are inherently transitory such that class claims may proceed despite mootness of the representative.

issues.label: Relation-back doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether class claims relate back to filing or certification to avoid mootness problems.

issues.label: Class claim mootness
issues.why: The court must determine whether any changes in government practice or circumstances moot the class controversy.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation
issues.why: If procedures changed during litigation, the court must assess whether the government’s cessation is voluntary and whether recurrence is reasonably expected.

issues.label: Ripeness
issues.why: The court must determine whether the declaratory claim is fit for judicial decision and not dependent on future contingent events for class members.

issues.label: Redressability of declaration
issues.why: The court must decide whether a declaratory judgment would likely remedy the alleged injury absent an injunction.

issues.label: Declaratory Judgment Act discretion
issues.why: Even with jurisdiction, the court must decide whether to exercise discretionary authority to issue declaratory relief.

issues.label: Advisory opinion bar
issues.why: The court must ensure the requested declaration resolves a concrete dispute and is not an impermissible advisory opinion.

issues.label: Rule 23(a) numerosity
issues.why: The court must reassess whether the class remains so numerous that joinder is impracticable.

issues.label: Rule 23(a) commonality
issues.why: The court must determine whether there are common questions capable of common resolution after Aleman Gonzalez and given requested declaratory relief.

issues.label: Rule 23(a) typicality
issues.why: The court must assess whether the representative’s claims are typical of the class, especially given his release and bond history.

issues.label: Rule 23(a) adequacy
issues.why: The court must confirm the representative and counsel will adequately protect the class’s interests.

issues.label: Rule 23(b)(2) requirements
issues.why: The court must decide whether defendants acted on grounds generally applicable to the class making final declaratory relief appropriate for the class as a whole.

issues.label: Indivisibility of relief
issues.why: The court must determine whether the requested declaration provides indivisible, classwide relief rather than individualized determinations.

issues.label: Need for individualized hearings
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether ability-to-pay and alternatives-to-detention issues require individualized factfinding incompatible with (b)(2) treatment.

issues.label: Ascertainability (implied)
issues.why: The court must ensure the class definition is administratively workable and objectively identifies members (even if not a formal requirement in all circuits).

issues.label: Class definition overbreadth
issues.why: The court must ensure the class is not defined in a way that includes uninjured persons or excludes injured ones.

issues.label: Decertification standard
issues.why: The court must apply the proper legal standard and evidentiary basis for modifying/decertifying a previously certified class.

issues.label: Effect of remedy limits on certification
issues.why: The court must decide whether loss of classwide injunctive relief under §1252(f)(1) undermines (b)(2) certification for declaratory relief.

issues.label: Manageability and supervision
issues.why: The court must consider whether the declaration would require ongoing judicial supervision akin to an injunction (relevant to §1252(f)(1) and DJA discretion).

issues.label: Due process framework
issues.why: The court must determine what procedural protections the Fifth Amendment requires for §1226(a) custody redetermination hearings.

issues.label: Burden allocation
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process permits placing the burden on the detainee under Matter of Guerra or requires the government to bear it.

issues.label: Standard of proof
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires clear-and-convincing evidence (vs preponderance) to justify continued detention.

issues.label: Danger/flight criteria
issues.why: The court must decide the constitutionally required substantive predicates (danger, flight risk, and possibly national security) for detention under §1226(a).

issues.label: Least restrictive conditions
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires a finding that no conditions of supervision can reasonably assure appearance and safety before continued detention.

issues.label: Ability-to-pay consideration
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires IJs to consider a detainee’s ability to pay when setting bond amount.

issues.label: Alternative conditions consideration
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires consideration of non-monetary alternatives to detention (parole-like conditions, supervision, etc.).

issues.label: Detention vs unaffordable bond
issues.why: The court must determine whether setting unaffordable bond without ability-to-pay analysis is unconstitutional as de facto detention.

issues.label: Procedural adequacy of IJ hearing
issues.why: The court must consider what procedural components are required (evidence, opportunity to present, reasons on record) for a constitutionally sufficient bond hearing.

issues.label: Agency discretion limits
issues.why: The court must reconcile due process requirements with the statutory delegation of discretionary detention decisions under §1226(a).

issues.label: Deference to BIA precedents
issues.why: The court must decide what weight to give Matter of Guerra/Barreiros in light of constitutional claims (Chevron/Brand X inapplicability to Constitution but relevant context).

issues.label: Facial vs as-applied claim
issues.why: The court must determine whether the class seeks a facial procedural rule or case-by-case relief and what standard governs such a challenge.

issues.label: Proper remedy for due process
issues.why: The court must determine whether a declaratory judgment can specify required procedures without exceeding judicial authority or intruding on agency adjudication.

issues.label: Habeas availability
issues.why: The court must determine whether habeas jurisdiction/remedy is available for class members’ custody challenges and how it interacts with declaratory relief.

issues.label: §2241 class habeas viability
issues.why: If proceeding in habeas, the court must consider whether class-wide habeas is permissible and what relief is available.

issues.label: Exhaustion requirements
issues.why: The court must decide whether class members must exhaust administrative remedies (IJ/BIA appeals) before seeking federal relief, and whether exhaustion is excused.

issues.label: Finality and timing
issues.why: The court must assess whether claims are premature for detainees who have not yet had hearings or who can seek IJ/BIA review.

issues.label: Prejudice requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs must show individualized prejudice from procedural defects to obtain declaratory relief for the pre-hearing class.

issues.label: Causation by challenged policy
issues.why: The court must decide whether the complained-of procedures stem from a uniform policy/practice attributable to defendants rather than IJ case-specific discretion.

issues.label: Effect of intervening precedent
issues.why: The court must apply Aleman Gonzalez and any relevant circuit precedents post-remand to both jurisdiction and remedy questions.

issues.label: Law of the case/mandate rule
issues.why: The court must determine what prior appellate rulings or stipulations constrain issues on remand.

issues.label: Justiciability after policy reversion
issues.why: Because procedures changed during the injunction period then reverted, the court must assess present controversy and likelihood of ongoing harm.

issues.label: Scope of declaration wording
issues.why: The court must decide how specific the declaration may be (burden, standard, factors) without becoming an enforcement injunction.

issues.label: Severability of requested components
issues.why: The court must decide whether burden/standard, ability-to-pay, and alternatives-to-detention are independent issues permitting partial declaratory relief.

issues.label: Rule 56 propriety
issues.why: For summary judgment, the court must decide whether material factual disputes exist regarding uniform practices, injury, and redressability.

issues.label: Record for classwide adjudication
issues.why: The court must determine whether the evidentiary record supports a classwide constitutional ruling rather than individualized development.

issues.label: Dismissal grounds
issues.why: The court must identify whether dismissal rests on lack of jurisdiction, mootness, failure to state a claim, or discretionary declination under the DJA.

issues.label: Form of dismissal
issues.why: The court must decide whether dismissal should be with or without prejudice depending on the basis (jurisdictional vs merits).

issues.label: Attorneys’ fees implications
issues.why: The court must consider whether any prevailing-party or equitable considerations affect fees if declaratory relief is granted or case dismissed.

issues.label: Notice and due process for decertification
issues.why: The court must consider whether any procedural protections or opportunities to be heard are required before decertifying a previously certified class.
